name: Yury Maksimov
forbes_bio: Yury Maksimov is the largest shareholder and cofounder of Positive Group, a Russian cybersecurity company.
Maksimov was trained as a physicist and initially worked for Russian noise measuring equipment developer Octava.
His older brother Dmitri worked at Russian bank SBS-Agro as a network security specialist and later wrote the XSpider program, which he posted on the Internet for free downloading.
As XSpider's popularity grew, in 2002, Dmitri and their friend Evgeny Kireev started Positive Technologies to further develop the program. Yury joined two years later.
In April 2021 the U.S. imposed sanctions against Positive along with five other Russian technology companies that provide cyber security services to the Russian government.
In December 2021 Positive Technologies went public in Moscow and was renamed to Positive Group.

name: Craig Abod
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Craig Abod is the founder and owner of Carahsoft, a Virginia-based technology company that specializes in IT services for government agencies.
Abod founded Carahsoft in 2004 and has grown the business to revenue of more than $11 billion.
Carahsoft ranked No. 20 on Forbes's 202 l5ist of America's Largest Private Companies.

name: Peng Jianhu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2018); Hurun Global (2017-2022); Hurun China (2016-2021)
forbes_bio: Peng Jianhu's fortune comes from his stake in Giant Network Group.
Giant changed its name from Chongqing New Century, a travel concern, after a backdoor listing of online game business Giant Interactive.
Peng graduated from Sichuan International Studies University as an English major.

name: Sergey Mikhaylov
forbes_bio: Sergey Mikhaylov inherited his fortune from his father, Igor Babaev, former managing director Cherkizovsky, a formerly state-owned meat-packing plant in Moscow.
Babaev became controlling shareholder of Cherkizovsky during Russia's privatization era in the 1990s, later adding pig and poultry farms, feed mills and other meat-packing plants.
Cherkizovo is now the largest meat producer in Russia, with 360,000 hectares (about 900,000 acres) of agricultural land.
Babaev retired from business in 2015 and gifted the shares to his two sons and ex-wife, who relinquished her shares in 2022.
Mikhaylov had internships with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley (USA) in the early 2000s.

name: Elizabeth Sy
forbes_bio: Elizabeth Sy is an advisor of SM Investments, a post she's held since 2012.
She is the second child of the late SM founder, Henry Sy.
She is president and chairman of SM Hotels and Conventions Corp., which oversees nine hotels including a slew of Radisson properties.
She started out as an assistant at her father's first hotel business, the Manila Royal Hotel.
She has a degree in business administration from Maryknoll College, now known as Miriam College.

name: He Jinhui
appears_on: Hurun China (2025-2026); Hurun Global (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2023-2024)

name: Chris Sacca
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2017-2021); Hurun Global (2020-2023)
forbes_bio: Chris Sacca made early bets investing in Twitter and Uber through his venture capital firm Lowercase Capital.
Sacca also invested in Twilio, a cloud software company, which went public in 2016.
In April 2017, Sacca announced he was retiring from venture capital to launch a podcast, act on TV shows and raise his young children.
Sacca also proclaimed himself an active opponent of the Trump administration.
forbes_facts: He is known for wearing cowboy shirts - a sharp detour from the Silicon Valley tech investor uniform.
He had a regular gig on the business pitch show Shark Tank; he stopped his appearances when he retired.

name: Francesco Saputo
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2023-2024); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Francesco Saputo owns a stake in his family's eponymous Canadian dairy company.
His father, Giuseppe, founded the business in 1954 with $500 and a bicycle for deliveries after immigrating to Canada from Sicily.
His brother, Emanuele (Lino) Saputo, was chairman from 1969 until retiring in 2017. His nephew, Lino, Jr., is the current chairman.
The publicly traded, Montreal-based company had revenues of $11.9 billion in 2022 and sells its products in more than 40 countries.

name: Kim Hyung-tae
forbes_bio: Kim Hyung-tae is the founder and CEO of Korean online game developer Shift Up.
He set up the firm in 2013 after working as a game artist at NCSoft, where he oversaw the design of the company's flagship online game Blade & Soul.
Shift Up's investors include Kakao Ventures, Smilegate Investment, Tencent and Wemade.
Shift Up's flagship game is Goddess of Victory: Nikke, a third-person shooter and role-playing game with anime-style graphics.
The company went public in July 2024, raising $320 million.

name: Ou Zongrong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2016-2021); Hurun Global (2014-2021); Hurun China (2006-2021)
forbes_bio: Ou Zongrong chairs the Zhenro Group, a real estate and infrastructure company long based in Fuzhou but now headquartered in Shanghai.
His brother Ou Zonghong, who chairs the Rongxin Group, is also a large China real estate developer.
